items.content_excerpt: $MSFT $GOOGL $NVDA Anthropic just dropped a pretty wild research note. They tested whether small open-source models can already set up and spread themselves across cheap consumer devices (think Android TV boxes, IoT stuff). Some Chinese open models stood out — Qwen handled unfamiliar hardware well, and GLM was the only one that completed the full self-replication chain in their tests. They’re estimating that by the end of 2026, even smaller models might reach this level. Open-source + self-spreading capability is a combination that feels genuinely new.

items.title: Microsoft reclaimed a $4 trillion market capitalization on Monday for the first time since October 2025, closing at $4.02 trillion as its sh
items.content_excerpt: Microsoft reclaimed a $4 trillion market capitalization on Monday for the first time since October 2025, closing at $4.02 trillion as its shares gained 1.14%. The milestone underscores the company’s recovery in investor confidence and brings it close to its all-time valuation record of $4.029 trillion, reached on Oct. 28, 2025. Microsoft last closed above the $4 trillion threshold on Oct. 29, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data. The achievement marks another step in Microsoft’s comeback as investors reassess its growth prospects and competitive position in the artificial intelligence market. Demand for AI infrastructure, cloud computing and enterprise software remains central to the company’s long-term outlook, although the timing and profitability of AI investments continue to shape sentiment across the technology sector. With its market value approaching a new record, Microsoft could soon establish a fresh milestone if its stock maintains its upward momentum. $MSFT

Anthropic looked at buying it for about 6 billion dollars and walked away in September after due diligence (Bloomberg). Talks can still fall apart, nothing is signed.

items.title: Wall Street’s dispersion trades face a critical test as major technology and semiconductor companies report earnings. Falling individual-sto
items.content_excerpt: Wall Street’s dispersion trades face a critical test as major technology and semiconductor companies report earnings. Falling individual-stock volatility has hurt the strategy, leaving some hedge funds with losses as both implied and realized volatility premiums relative to the S&P 500 have narrowed. Traders hope earnings surprises, particularly around AI demand and semiconductor capital spending, will trigger stronger stock-specific movements. Dispersion strategies typically involve buying volatility in individual stocks while selling index volatility, betting that companies will move differently. Adapt Investment Managers’ Alexis Maubourguet said positions rebuilt after July’s pullback are now under pressure as investor conviction in AI-driven gains weakens. UBS strategist Kieran Diamond noted that options markets are pricing in the largest single-day earnings reactions since the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly for technology stocks. $SPX $UBS $NVDA $AMZN

Meta said Muse Wonder will soon power its Muse AI agent, potentially expanding AI capabilities across the company’s products and services. The new models could help Meta improve user engagement, deliver more sophisticated AI-driven experiences and develop additional monetization opportunities across its digital ecosystem. Analysts expect the launch to create new business prospects as companies increasingly seek advanced AI tools and agents capable of handling more complex tasks. $META

items.content_excerpt: $MSFT $GOOGL $NVDA Anthropic just dropped a pretty wild research note. items.title: Google successfully launched its prototype Project Suncatcher satellite into space aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare mission, confirm
items.content_excerpt: Google successfully launched its prototype Project Suncatcher satellite into space aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare mission, confirming that contact has been established and the satellite is operating as expected. Developed in collaboration with Planet, the initiative explores whether space could eventually support large-scale machine-learning infrastructure, potentially expanding the locations where AI computing systems can operate. Over the coming weeks, Google will collect orbital data to evaluate how its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) withstand the physical stresses of spaceflight, including extreme radiation and temperature fluctuations. The company emphasized that some of these tests can only be conducted in the space environment, making the mission an important step in assessing the technical feasibility of space-based AI computing. $GOOGL $SPCX

items.content_excerpt: Alphabet and Google unveiled the $180 Fitbit Edge, a premium fitness tracker replacing the Fitbit Charge 6 and targeting the gap between screenless wearables and full-featured smartwatches. The device features a larger display, improved location tracking, broader contextual activity recognition and a modular design with a replaceable battery, positioning it between the screenless Fitbit Air and the flagship Pixel Watch. The launch supports Google’s strategy to expand its subscription-based Google Health ecosystem and recurring revenue. Buyers receive three months of Google Health Premium, normally $10 per month, featuring generative AI coaching and advanced health monitoring, including trend analysis for metrics such as insulin resistance and blood pressure. Google also expanded data-sharing partnerships with Abbott, Flo Health, MyFitnessPal and Function Health. Preorders are open ahead of the October 27 commercial launch. $GOOGL

After approximately $570,000 in quarterly revenue, the key question is whether accelerating optical engine shipments and customer qualification programs will translate into measurable revenue growth. items.content_excerpt: $POET 3. items.content_excerpt: $POET 2. The Operational Mirage (No Real Manufacturing Footprint) • The Headcount Impossibility: The company operates globally with fewer than 100 total employees. items.title: U.S. banks will kick off third-quarter earnings season on Tuesday and Wednesday, offering investors the first major insight into how rising
items.content_excerpt: U.S. banks will kick off third-quarter earnings season on Tuesday and Wednesday, offering investors the first major insight into how rising Treasury yields, higher oil prices and economic uncertainty are affecting businesses and consumers. Results from the six largest U.S. banks will be closely scrutinized for signs of weakening loan demand, slower economic activity and changes in consumer and corporate borrowing. Investors will focus on year-over-year improvements, as the previous quarter benefited from unusually strong IPO activity that boosted investment-banking revenue, potentially making sequential comparisons less meaningful. Bank earnings are considered a key indicator of broader economic and stock-market health because banks finance corporate expansion and consumer spending, including purchases of homes and cars. $BAC $JPM $C $WFC

items.content_excerpt: Bank of America upgraded Salesforce to Buy from Underperform and raised its price target to $285 from $160, implying approximately 24% upside from its latest closing price of $229.13. Analyst Tal Liani said concerns that artificial intelligence could disintermediate traditional software providers have eased following discussions with CIOs and other market participants. Large enterprises are unlikely to replace platforms that manage critical business logic, data, workflows and regulatory compliance; instead, AI could deepen their dependence on these systems. Liani highlighted Salesforce’s four-layer enterprise AI architecture: its data layer provides regulated context, Sales Cloud and Service Cloud manage business logic and workflows, Agentforce delivers AI reasoning and orchestration, and Slack and Anthropic-powered Claudeforce enable natural-language interaction. $CRM $BAC
